title: ESC deselect is undone by the drag-release click-select (press_swallowed never checked on the drag-release path)
evidence:
app/main.odin:337:
		app.press_swallowed = true // an in-flight click's release must not re-select after ESC
app/main.odin:492-494:
			moved := rl.Vector2Distance(mouse, app.press) > 6
			if !moved && !release_ui_hit(app, mouse) {
				click_select(app, mouse)
			}
detail: The drag-release click-select path (492-494) never checks press_swallowed, unlike the plain-release branch (524). Press a node, hit ESC, release without moving: the node re-selects, undoing the ESC deselect the comment and PR body promise.
recommended_fix: Gate the drag-release click_select on !app.press_swallowed, matching the plain-release branch: if !moved && !app.press_swallowed && !release_ui_hit(app, mouse) { click_select(app, mouse) }

title: PR interaction map claims chord release cannot re-select, but code explicitly enables it
detail: The PR interaction map says the chord's release cannot re-select; the code sets press_swallowed = false so the release DOES click-select (fresh anchor). Documented contract contradicts the implementation.
recommended_fix: Either swallow the chord release (press_swallowed = true) or fix the PR interaction-map row to say the chord's release click-selects with a fresh anchor.

title: Demolish-node rejection toast can never render (toast drawn only inside the sel_pipe >= 0 block)
evidence:
app/main.odin:1022:
	if app.sel_pipe >= 0 {
app/main.odin:1062-1063:
		if app.last_reject != .None && app.tick - app.reject_tick < 30 { // ~1.5s at 20Hz
			draw_text(app, reject_label(app.last_reject), 12, 156, 16, rl.Color{200, 60, 60, 255})
detail: demolish_node failures keep sel_node >= 0 with sel_pipe == -1, so this toast never renders; the PR's '.Missing_Node / .Terminal_Demolish -> last_reject toast' belt-and-braces surface has no render path for node-only selections.
recommended_fix: Draw the reject toast outside the sel_pipe block (gated only on last_reject freshness), so node-demolish rejections also surface.

title: popover_rect tray clamp overflows small windows, contradicting its own comment
detail: A 120px-high window with the 92px node popover gives y = 120-46-92 = -18, and min() keeps it — panel overflows the top. Same for x when win_w < POPOVER_W + 16. Contradicts the adjacent comment.
recommended_fix: Clamp after the tray clamp: y = max(8, min(y, f32(v.win_h) - h - 8)); x = max(8, min(x, f32(v.win_w) - POPOVER_W - 8)).
